interpretations.sentence: Those involved in COVID care had a higher mean stress score (52.16 ± 22.41 versus 38.60 ± 19.55; p=0.005) and a higher mean burnout score (58.30 ± 23.54 vs. 47.06 ± 23.40; p=0.033) compared to those not involved in COVID care.
interpretations.claim: Psychiatrists involved in COVID care had significantly higher stress scores than those not involved.

interpretations.sentence: Another unexpected finding was regarding the professional groups: only among psychiatrists did we find that their participation in COVID care was associated with an increase in stress and burnout scores.
interpretations.claim: Participation in COVID care was associated with increased stress scores only among psychiatrists.
